artists.biography: CIV was a hardcore punk band from New York City. The band is named after its vocalist, Anthony Civarelli. Three of the band's members (Civarelli, Siegler and Smilios) were members of Gorilla Biscuits. Band member Siegler played in other hardcore bands, including Youth of Today, Judge and Gorilla Biscuits.

perplexity.description:
Set Your Goals" is the debut studio album by New York punk band CIV, originally released in 1995 on Lava Records (the album's widely cited original release year is October 1995).

Musically, the record blends melodic punk and hardcore-influenced pop-punk, featuring short, hook-driven songs built on aggressive yet accessible guitar work and singalong choruses that reflect singer CIV's Hardcore/Punk roots while leaning toward radio-friendly punk songcraft. The album’s sound sits between East Coast hardcore lineage and mid‑90s mainstream punk production, and includes a notable cover of SSD's "Glue" that appears on certain vinyl pressings originally issued via Revelation Records in 1996.

In the band's discography, Set Your Goals functions as CIV's breakthrough and defining statement as their debut LP, establishing their identity after members’ earlier involvement in the hardcore scene and leading into subsequent releases. Critical and commercial responses at the time recognized its catchy, punk-pop orientation and helped the band gain wider visibility in the mid‑1990s punk boom; sources commonly cite the 1995 release as the starting point for CIV's broader recognition and note later vinyl pressings and reissues handled by Revelation Records in 1996.
